summary: Extends PPP's vendor extensions to cover vendor-specific Network, Authentication and Control Protocols. Earlier work already allowed vendor-specific options and codes in the Link Control Protocol. This extends that idea.

eli5.summary: A phone line protocol let companies add their own options. This lets them add their own protocols in more places too.

questions: what is the ppp vendor protocol
what is an oui in ppp
subtitle: Four reserved PPP protocol numbers that let vendors run their own network, control and authentication protocols.

tldr.problem: Vendors who want proprietary network or authentication protocols over PPP had to switch them on through LCP, before the peer was authenticated, using protocol numbers IANA had not assigned.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC reserves one protocol number in each of PPP's four protocol ranges (005b, 405b, 805b, c05b). Each message carries the vendor's three-octet OUI so peers know whose protocol it is.
tldr.outcome: Vendors get a clean, standard place to hang proprietary protocols, and monitoring tools can recognise the fixed numbers. The security of each vendor protocol is still up to the vendor.

today: RFC 3772 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 2153, and IANA has assigned the four protocol values it describes.

sections.title: Why Vendor Protocols Need Their Own Numbers
sections.content:
The PPP Vendor Extensions already let vendors add proprietary options and Code values to the Link Control Protocol (LCP). Some implementors also want whole proprietary network and control protocols. They could enable such a protocol with the LCP Vendor-Specific Option and then negotiate it using a locally assigned protocol number, but the RFC names three problems with that staged approach.

  • LCP negotiation happens before the peer has been identified and authenticated, which complicates the security analysis.
  • With compulsory tunneling, the system doing the first LCP negotiation may be unrelated to the system that uses the proprietary protocol.
  • A protocol number not assigned by IANA makes life harder for diagnostic tools, which can show a fixed number in a reasonable, if limited, format.
sections.eli5: Before, a company had to sneak its secret game rules in before anyone showed ID, and nobody could tell what the game was called. Now there are official, labelled slots.

sections.title: Four Reserved Protocol Numbers
sections.content:
The cleaner solution is a set of vendor-specific protocols, one in each of the four protocol number ranges defined by RFC 1661. The RFC reserves these values.

  • 005b: Vendor-Specific Network Protocol (VSNP)
  • 405b: Vendor-Specific Protocol (VSP)
  • 805b: Vendor-Specific Network Control Protocol (VSNCP)
  • c05b: Vendor-Specific Authentication Protocol (VSAP)

Each message carries a three-octet OUI, the Organizationally Unique Identifier of the vendor that defines the meaning of the message. A vendor's own data follows the OUI, and the RFC places no restrictions on it for VSNP.
sections.eli5: There are four numbered slots, each for a different kind of job. Every note put in a slot has the company's name on it.

sections.title: VSNCP and VSNP: Vendor Network Layer
sections.content:
VSNCP negotiates the use of VSNP. It uses the same packet exchange and option negotiation mechanism as LCP, but with a different set of options. Exactly one VSNCP packet is carried in the PPP Information field, with the PPP Protocol field set to hex 805b.

The packet has Code, Identifier, Length, a three-octet OUI and Data. Only LCP Code values 1 through 7 are used (Configure-Request, Configure-Ack, Configure-Nak, Configure-Reject, Terminate-Request, Terminate-Ack and Code-Reject); all other codes SHOULD result in a VSNCP Code-Reject reply.

VSNCP packets MUST NOT be exchanged until PPP has reached the Network-Layer Protocol phase, and ones received earlier MUST be silently ignored. An unrecognized OUI SHOULD draw an LCP Protocol-Reject. VSNP packets, with Protocol field 005b, MUST NOT be sent unless VSNCP is in the Opened state.
sections.eli5: First the two sides agree, politely, that they will use a company's special language. Only after they both say yes do they start sending messages in it.

sections.title: VSP: Per-Link Vendor Messages
sections.content:
The Vendor-Specific Protocol (VSP) is meant for cases where a full network layer protocol is unnecessary, or where per-link signaling is required. It uses Protocol field value 405b and carries exactly one packet in the Information field.

The packet holds a four-octet Magic-Number, a three-octet OUI, a one-octet Reserved field and Data. The Magic-Number detects looped-back links; if the LCP Magic-Number Option was not negotiated, it MUST be set to 0, and implementing that option is RECOMMENDED. Reserved MUST be zero on transmit and is ignored on reception.

VSP packets MUST NOT be sent until PPP has reached the Network-Layer Protocol or Authentication phase, and earlier arrivals MUST be silently ignored. After that, a VSP packet with an unrecognized OUI SHOULD be returned using LCP Protocol-Reject.
sections.eli5: VSP is a quick note passed along one single road, with no big agreement needed first. The note carries a tag so the sender can tell if their own note came right back.

sections.title: VSAP: Vendor Authentication
sections.content:
The Vendor-Specific Authentication Protocol (VSAP) is used in two ways. First, an LCP Authentication Option negotiates a vendor-specific authentication protocol for the Authentication phase. Second, VSAP packets carry the proprietary authentication messages during that phase.

The option appears in LCP Configure-Request, -Ack, -Nak and -Reject. Its Type is 3, its Length is 7 or more, and the Authentication-Protocol field is hex c05b in network byte order, followed by the OUI and optional Data.

The authentication data has Code, Identifier, Length and Data. The vendor defines Code, Data and the processing. The RFC does RECOMMEND Code 3 for Success and Code 4 for Failure, as with CHAP (RFC 1994) and EAP (RFC 2284), to simplify network monitoring equipment.
sections.eli5: Some companies have their own secret handshake to prove who you are. This lets them use it, and suggests the same words for yes and no that other handshakes use.

sections.title: OUIs and Multiple Vendors
sections.content:
The OUI is based on IEEE 802 vendor assignments. Vendors using their IEEE OUI SHOULD also register it with IANA. A vendor without an IEEE OUI, such as a software-only vendor, can request a PPP-specific OUI from IANA, assigned from the CF0000 series.

An implementation MAY support more than one vendor protocol, told apart by OUI. It MUST then handle LCP Protocol-Reject specially, reading the OUI in the rejected message and disabling only that protocol, not all use of the vendor number. This stays compatible with simple implementations that support one OUI. The mechanism is expected only for cooperating vendors, and vendors are encouraged to use a single OUI for all their protocols.
sections.eli5: The company name tag comes from an official list. If a company has no tag yet, it can ask for one from a special set.

sections.title: Multilink, Compression and Encryption
sections.content:
VSNP operates at the bundle level if Multilink PPP is in use, and above any compression and encryption protocols in use.

VSP operates at the per-link level under Multilink PPP and MUST NOT be subjected to data compression. If a per-link encryption protocol is in use, VSP packets MUST be encrypted. Because VSP is per-link, bundle-level encryption does not affect it.
sections.eli5: One kind of message travels with the whole group of roads, and the other travels on just one road, so they get treated differently.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security of a vendor authentication protocol depends on that proprietary mechanism. An implementation wanting to avoid such problems SHOULD send LCP Configure-Nak in response to a Configure-Request specifying VSAP, or MAY terminate operation.

When PPP encryption is used without Multilink PPP, VSP packets are sent in the clear. Implementations that need PPP encryption for security should consider per-link encryption or using VSNP instead of VSP. Vendor networking protocols are also only as secure as their own mechanisms, and independent analysis is RECOMMENDED.

VSP can travel unencrypted when only PPP encryption (without Multilink PPP) is in use.
sections.eli5: A secret handshake is only as safe as the company that made it up, so you can politely say no thanks. And one kind of note may not be locked up, so check first.
